key_insight: Controlled solvent/antisolvent etching creates rectangular cavities inside layered halide perovskite microcrystals for regrowing compositionally distinct, endo-epitaxial heterostructures.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a chemical route to designed internal perovskite interfaces without conventional lithography, although solar-cell performance is not demonstrated in the abstract.
method: Etch from the top surface preferentially along crystallographic [100] and [010] directions.
Tune cavities through etching time, temperature, and etchant composition, with interruptible etching cycles.
Regrow distinct layered perovskites inside cavities using sequential precursor addition.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports tunable cavity formation, stepwise etching, and confined regrowth across diverse perovskite compositions and antisolvent systems, but provides no quantitative metrics.
watch_item: Reproducible interface quality and compatibility with photovoltaic device fabrication remain to be established.
paper_title: Solvent/Antisolvent-Driven Etching of 2D Layered Halide Perovskite Microcrystals toward Endo-Epitaxial Heterostructures
